details.description: Llama 3.2 90B Vision Instruct is the largest model in Meta's Llama 3.2 family, released September 25, 2024. It pairs a separately trained vision adapter (using cross-attention layers) with the Llama 3.1 text backbone, so it can reason over images alongside text for tasks such as visual question answering, document understanding and chart reading. Text-only prompts support eight languages, but Meta states that image-plus-text prompts are English only. AWS Bedrock's own model card lists this model's lifecycle as Legacy, with a stated EOL date of July 7, 2026, which has already passed as of this research.
advantages: Scores 90.1% (ANLS) on DocVQA and 85.5% relaxed accuracy on ChartQA (CoT), per Meta's model card.
Scores 92.3% on AI2 Diagram and 78.1% on VQAv2, per Meta's model card.
Scores 60.3% on MMMU (CoT) for multimodal reasoning and 57.3% on MathVista, per Meta's model card.
Scores 86.0% on MMLU and 68.0% on MATH (CoT) for its text-only capabilities, per Meta's model card.
Supports eight text-only languages (English, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Spanish, Thai), per Meta's model card.
disadvantages: Image-plus-text prompts are English only; the other supported languages apply to text-only use, per Meta's model card.
Knowledge cutoff of December 2023, per Meta's model card.
Meta's model card does not describe tool-calling or function-calling support for this model.

AWS Bedrock's model card lists this model's lifecycle as Legacy, with a stated EOL date of July 7, 2026 that has already passed as of this research (2026-09-24), though the page has not been updated to show an EOL status.
use_cases: Document understanding and reading of charts, diagrams and scanned documents
Multilingual text-only assistant chat in the eight supported languages

notes: AWS Bedrock's own model card (fetched 2026-09-24) shows this model's lifecycle as 'Legacy' with a stated 'Model EOL date: July 7, 2026' -- a date already in the past relative to today, even though the page still labels the model Legacy rather than EOL; this may mean the page has not been updated, or that access is already restricted. Meta's own model card does not describe the model as deprecated. The catalog's modality (image_input, text_input, text_output), max_input_tokens (128000) and max_output_tokens (4096) match what both Meta and AWS Bedrock state.
